hook: Yes, it's about cake. The tone is completely deadpan, and the joke and the threat turn out to be the same thing, so don't decide too early whether you're reading a comedy. The containment procedures are both the funniest and the grimmest part, and they only fully make sense once you reach the final paragraph.
whyItMatters: 871 is a good example of the harmless-object, catastrophic-math style: nothing in it is frightening on its own, but runaway growth turns a dessert into a planetary problem. It shows how much the format can do by following one simple rule all the way to its end. The idea that a Keter is held back only by people sitting down and eating, day after day, is a big part of its charm.
thingsToNotice: The danger is held back until the very end, so the locked cells and armed escorts look absurd until the 80-day estimate lands. Notice the small touches that keep it light, like the range of cakes, the giant baumkuchen and the site-wide ban on desserts. Underneath the gag, the procedures also show how casually D-class staff are treated, which leaves a sour aftertaste. The note that instances slowly 'mutate' adds a quiet open question about where the cakes are heading.

related.note: Another self-replicating object, though there the fix is restraint rather than cooperation.
A kitchen-counter anomaly whose everyday premise hides how strange things can get.
